extracted.name: Crispy chicken po’ boy
extracted.description: Have you ever made a sandwich that is so generously stuffed that you know from the beginning you're going to need both hands? That's exactly what this Crispy Chicken Po’ Boy is. It's not one of those delicate little sandwiches that you can politely nibble at. This one is loaded with crunchy golden chicken, fresh lettuce, red onion, ketchup and a creamy, slightly spicy sauce, all tucked into a soft sesame bun. And honestly? That's the perfect combination. One bite gives you crunchy chicken, creamy sauce, fresh vegetables all at once. And that's what makes a good Po’ Boy so irresistible. Serve it with hot fries and an ice-cold drink, and you've got a homemade fast-food meal that might just make you forget about ordering takeout. #CookpadApron2026
ingredient_lines: 1/2 kg Boneless chicken breast, cut into strips or bite-size pieces
instruction_lines: Marinate the chicken: Combine buttermilk, hot sauce, salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and cayenne. Add chicken and mix well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Prepare the coating: Combine flour, cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, pepper, salt, cayenne and baking powder.
Remove each chicken piece from the buttermilk and let the excess drip off. Press firmly into the seasoned flour.

For extra-crispy chicken, dip it back into the buttermilk and coat in the flour a second time. Heat oil to 350°F/175°C. Fry the chicken in batches for 4–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown.
Drain on a wire rack and season with a tiny pinch of salt while hot.
Make the sauce: Mix everything together and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.
Build the Po’ Boy: Lightly toast the bread.
Spread the creamy sauce generously on both sides.
Add plenty of lettuce, red onion. Pile the crispy chicken on top.
Finish with another drizzle of sauce and a little ketchup if you like.
Serve immediately with crispy fries and a cold drink.
